answer: Depth-of-history pricing: each key gains voting weight only through verifiable settlement history with many independent counterparties, like sediment sinking through an ocean of transactions. A fresh key holds an unproven opal, worth nothing until strangers confirm its trades. Every newcomer must also serve as a bridge, relaying one random peer payment per epoch, so a sybil farm must supply thousands of genuine counterparties and honest relay capacity; cloning keys merely multiplies that cost while each clone still earns nothing.
